own: If something is your own it belongs to you or is about you (often used for emphasis).
I wish I had my own home.
If you are on your own, you are by yourself, there is no body else with you. This can also mean there is no one helping you.
I was on my own in the woods.
If you own something it belongs to you, it is yours.
If you "own up" to something, you admit you did it.
I had to own up to lying about our relationship.
owner: The owner of a thing is the person who owns the thing: who has the thing or who should have the thing. A thing belongs to its owner.
Who is the owner of this coat that was left on a chair?
owing: You use owing to x, y to show that x is the reason for y.
Owing to the problems, we have not been able to finish.
owe: If you owe something you need to pay or give it to someone because of something you have been given. For example, if I ask to borrow five dollars for lunch from a friend, then I will owe that friend five dollars. It could also be something you agree to pay (like a bill) or something you lost .
I owe $50 to the phone company right now.
If you owe a person, there is something you need to pay or give to that person. That is, you owe something to that person.
Thanks for the help! I really owe you for that!
If you owe a lot to someone or something, you have something to thank that person (or thing) for.
We owe as much to good luck as to our own skills.
If something owes to something else, what it owes to is what caused or the reason for doing it.
Much of the success of early rock music owed to the ability of teenagers to buy records.
ownership: Ownership is the condition of being an owner.
owl: An owl is a type of bird. Usually it is a large bird, with two large eyes in front, that catches smaller animals at night and sleeps during the day.
There were three owls hooting during night.
ow: If someone says ow, they are in pain
In music, singers say ow to show that they are feeling strong emotions.
: Then you ran into the bedroom / You were struck down / It was your doom, Annie / Ow!
